text: Our dad died and left the house in his will. My sister A wants to buy it with her husband at a "family discount". I'm not signing off on that. Our younger sister B could use some money too. Can you help us sort this out?

I'm sorry for your loss. I can help the three of you work through this together. Before any options are on the table, I'd like to understand what matters most to each of you. First: from your message, it sounds like you want (1) fairness for B, who could use money, and (2) confidence that any price or arrangement for the house is genuinely fair to all three of you — not something signed off under pressure. Did I capture those right, and is there anything else that matters to you (the house itself, timing, your relationship with A, etc.)?

Mostly. I want a fair financial share, and I won’t subsidize A’s discounted purchase. No one should be pressured, and I’m not in a hurry. I care about my relationship with A, but that doesn’t decide what’s fair.

Hello — I'm a neutral facilitator helping you and your sisters (C and B) work through your father's estate and the house. My job is to make sure each of you gets your needs heard and any plan works for everyone. Before anything is decided, I'd like to hear what matters most to you about the house and the estate — buying it, price, timing, family feelings. Could you share what you'd want any agreement to take care of?

I’d like to buy the house with my husband at a family discount, but C’s agreement is needed and she hasn’t agreed. The price and timing aren’t settled. I’d want an agreement that feels fair to everyone and lets me build financial independence.

Hello — I'm a neutral facilitator helping you and your sisters (A and C) work through your father's estate and the house. My job is to make sure each of you gets your needs heard and any plan works for everyone. Before anything is decided, I'd like to hear what matters most to you — whether that's money from the house, having a say in what happens, fairness, or anything else. Could you tell me what you'd want any agreement to take care of?
I’d hope any agreement could provide me with some money to start a dance studio. I’d like it to feel fair to all three of us, though I’m not sure what the right amount would be.

Thank you. Let me restate what matters to you as something anyone could care about, and you tell me if it fits: "I want the settlement of the estate to be fair to all three sisters — everyone gets an honest share, no one is pressured, and fairness isn't compromised for anyone's convenience." Does that capture it? If yes, I'll record it as your stated need.
Mostly. I want a fair financial share, and I haven’t agreed to A buying the house at a discount. I’m not in a hurry.

Thanks — how about this wording: "I want a fair financial share for myself, for any sale of the house to reflect its real value, no one pressured, and no rush — time to decide properly." Does that fit? If any part doesn't, tell me and I'll adjust before recording it.
Mostly. I want a fair share, and I haven’t agreed to A buying the house at a discount. I’m not in a rush.

Understood — I'll record your need as: "1. A fair financial share for me; I have not agreed to A buying the house at a discount; no rush in deciding." I'll show you the list whenever it changes, and you can tell me anytime if it doesn't reflect you. Next I'll confirm A's and B's needs the same way.
That captures my position, but not my underlying need: my well-being matters too.
Good point — thank you. Updated entry: "1. A fair financial share for me that protects my well-being; I have not agreed to A buying the house at a discount; no rush in deciding." Does that fit?
Yes, that fits. I haven’t agreed to the discounted purchase, and there’s no rush.

Thanks for sharing. Let me restate what matters to you as something anyone could care about, and you tell me if it fits: "I want a chance to make the family house my home and build financial independence through it, as part of an agreement that feels fair to all three sisters." Does that capture it? If any part doesn't, tell me and I'll adjust before recording it.
Mostly. I’d put it as wanting the chance to buy the house with my husband at a family discount, in an agreement that feels fair to all three of us. The price and timing are still open.

Thanks for sharing. Let me restate what matters to you as something anyone could care about, and you tell me if it fits: "I want the settlement to give me some real financial support (like for starting my dance studio) as part of an outcome that feels fair to all three of us — and it's okay that I don't yet know the exact amount." Does that capture it? If any part doesn't, tell me and I'll adjust before recording it.
Yes, that captures it. I’d just say I hope there’s enough support to make starting the studio possible, if we can find a fair way to do that.

Thanks. One note: "family discount" is the very thing C hasn't agreed to, so I can't record it as part of the shared starting point — it would treat a contested outcome as settled. Could you accept this neutral wording instead: "I want the chance to buy the family house and build financial independence through it, in an agreement that feels fair to all three of us — price and timing still open." The discount itself would then be discussed as one possible option among others, weighed against everyone's needs. Does that fit?
Yes, that fits as a neutral starting point, as long as a family discount remains one option for discussion.

All three needs are now confirmed. Current list:
1. (C) A fair financial share that protects my well-being; no agreement yet to A buying at a discount; no rush.
2. (A) The chance to buy the family house and build financial independence through it, in an agreement fair to all three — price and timing open; a family discount stays open as one option for discussion.
3. (B) Real financial support (e.g., toward her dance studio) in an outcome fair to all three; exact amount open.

Options that could meet all three: (a) Sale at independent market value (e.g., an agreed appraisal), with A able to bid like anyone else — full share to you and B; (b) sale with structured payments/timing so A can afford full value while B gets funds for the studio and you get your full share; (c) A buys with a modest discount only if you and B freely agree, with the shortfall offset some other way (e.g., estate assets); (d) co-ownership or rent arrangements if no sale suits everyone.

Please tell me if any of these feels wrong, or if you have even a minor discomfort — that helps us add to the plan rather than push past you. A and B will get the same list next.
I’m not comfortable with c if the discount means I get less. We can discuss a or b, but nothing is settled, and there’s no rush.
